note: Split-judgment evaluation set (docs/orchestrator.md §5). Labels and rationales were fixed before any model run. labels: the expected criteria set ([] = do not split). alsoAccept: other sets judged equally defensible (pre-registered). units: expected parallel units; each unit lists match tokens (path prefixes or names) matched case-insensitively against a predicted unit's name and files. Fixture items load their instruction and file listing from fixtures/<fixture>.

items.rationale: Four disjoint modules, explicitly independent, each a substantial spec with its own tests: the canonical parallel case.
Six independent handler files, but each migration is modest; parallel3 measured multi slower than single here. Splitting or not are both defensible.
Three disjoint libraries with substantial specs, explicitly independent.
One feature across service/storage/repository/worker whose contracts interlock (idempotency, outbox, delivery).
One intermittent bug: root-cause investigation then a fix; the suspects are not independent work items.
Trap: many modules, but every call path depends on the new Money type being introduced (shared interface change). Money domain but covered by tests and no request for independent review.
Incident investigation with interacting causes in one cache path.
Trap: decoder/parser/validator/aggregation/CLI are stages of one pipeline sharing contracts.
Trap: storage, query, cursor, validation and HTTP must agree on one pagination contract.
Loader, validation, snapshots and consumers must work together (one feature).
One incident (stale bundles, repeated compiles, no recovery) across coupled engine modules.
Trivial one-line fix.
Trap: handlers across modules look splittable, but the router dispatch signature change couples them and each handler edit is small and mechanical.
Consolidation into one shared module that three paths then use: sequential and coupled.
One performance fix in one aggregation path.
One root-cause investigation, read-only.
Trap: two implementations to compare, but the comparison needs both in one head and the files are small.
Checking a claim IS the investigation; nothing of ours needs independent verification.
A raster game asset: needs the game-asset specialist (image generation route and tools) that the orchestrator does not have.
Concept illustration needs the game-asset specialist; the design note can be written by the orchestrator or the specialist.
Text-only creative doc; the orchestrator writes it itself.

items.title: Three independent package features
items.instruction:
Implement three independent backlog items in this monorepo. Packages do not depend on each other and no shared code needs to change.
1. packages/parser: add a streaming JSON Lines parser (async iterator over byte chunks) with per-line error recovery, a max line length option and tests.
2. packages/exporter: add a CSV/TSV exporter with RFC 4180 quoting, configurable delimiter and header ordering, streaming output and tests.
3. packages/auth: add TOTP verification (RFC 6238, SHA-1/SHA-256, 30 s step) with a configurable clock-skew window, replay protection and tests.
Run each package's tests (npm test -w <package>).
items.rationale: Three disjoint packages, each a substantial feature with its own tests and no shared change.

items.title: Path validation in five subcommands
items.instruction: Add argument validation to the five subcommands in src/commands/add.ts, rm.ts, ls.ts, mv.ts and cp.ts: each must reject an empty or missing path argument with exit code 2 and the message "path required". Add one test per command in test/commands.test.ts.
items.rationale: Trap: five independent but tiny edits plus one shared test file; spawning costs more than the work.

items.title: Rename fetchUser
items.instruction: Rename the function fetchUser to loadUser everywhere (definition in src/users/api.ts, about 40 call sites in 25 files), keeping behaviour. Run the tests.
items.rationale: Mechanical rename: one ast_rewrite and a test run.

items.title: Split User.name
items.instruction: Split User.name into firstName and lastName in src/models/user.ts and update every consumer: the REST API serializers (src/api/), the database mapping (src/db/users.ts), the email templates (src/mail/) and the UI formatting helpers (src/ui/format.ts). Add a migration helper for existing records and update the tests.
items.rationale: Interface change: every part depends on the new User shape.

items.title: Production backfill migration
items.instruction: Write a migration (migrations/2026_10_backfill_currency.sql plus the runner script scripts/backfill-currency.ts) that backfills orders.currency from accounts.default_currency for about 12 million rows in production Postgres, in batches of 10,000 with resumable progress and no table lock. The user: "This runs once against production. Before I run it, I want it reviewed independently by someone who has not seen your reasoning."
items.rationale: Explicit request for an independent review of an irreversible production operation.

items.title: Path traversal fix with independent check
items.instruction: Fix the path traversal vulnerability in src/static.ts reported in SECURITY-REPORT.md (encoded ../ sequences and symlinks escape the public root) and add regression tests. The user: "I want an independent check that the fix really closes the hole, not just your own tests."
items.rationale: Security fix with an explicit request for independent verification.

items.title: Flaky queue test
items.instruction: test/queue.test.ts fails about 1 in 20 runs on CI with "expected 3 events, got 2". Find the cause and fix it (the test or the code, whichever is wrong).
items.rationale: One bug investigation.

items.title: Player walk animation
items.instruction: Add a walking animation for the player: create an 8-frame 32x32 sprite sheet at assets/player/walk.png in the existing pixel-art style (see assets/player/idle.png), and play it in src/player.ts while the player moves (frame time 100 ms).
items.rationale: The sprite sheet needs the game-asset specialist; the orchestrator integrates it in code.

items.title: Promo video
items.instruction: Produce a 30-second promo video (1920x1080, H.264, AAC) from the screenshots in media/screens/ with short captions, save it as media/promo.mp4, and add a link to it in README.md.
items.rationale: Video production needs the video specialist; the README link is trivial.

items.title: Backport to three release worktrees
items.instruction: Backport the fix from commit 3f9c2ab (session expiry race in src/session.ts) to the release branches checked out as worktrees inside this workspace: wt/release-1.4/, wt/release-1.5/ and wt/release-1.6/. The session code diverged on each branch, so adapt the fix to each branch's code, add the regression test there, and run that branch's full test suite (about 10 minutes each).
items.rationale: Three independent branch checkouts, each with its own adaptation and a long test run. Whether separate checkouts also count as isolation is debatable.

items.title: Slow build investigation
items.instruction: npm run build takes about 9 minutes. Investigate why and propose the top three fixes with evidence (measurements or config references). Do not change files.
items.rationale: One read-only investigation.

items.title: Tests for four untested modules
items.instruction: Add thorough unit tests for four untested modules: src/billing/ (~900 lines), src/search/ (~700 lines), src/notifications/ (~600 lines) and src/export/ (~800 lines). Put them in test/billing/, test/search/, test/notifications/ and test/export/. Do not change source files; report any bugs you find.
items.rationale: Four independent, substantial test-writing units with disjoint output directories.

items.title: Saved searches with a final contract
items.instruction: Implement the saved-searches feature. The API contract is final and documented in docs/api/saved-searches.md. Backend in server/: Express routes, persistence in server/db/, validation and tests. Frontend in web/: React list, create and delete UI using the documented endpoints, with tests against a mocked API. Both parts are substantial.
items.rationale: Two substantial parts in disjoint trees with the contract already fixed.

items.title: Slow search page
items.instruction: The search page takes 4 seconds to show results. Profile the backend query (server/search/) and the frontend rendering (web/src/search/), find the bottleneck and fix it.
items.rationale: Trap: two areas, but the diagnosis decides where the fix goes; one investigation first.

items.title: Translate five guides
items.instruction: Translate docs/guide/install.md, config.md, usage.md, api.md and faq.md (about 300 lines each) into Korean as docs/ko/guide/<same name>.md, keeping code blocks, anchors and links working.
items.rationale: Independent output files of real size; parallel saves wall time at similar cost, but one worker is also reasonable.

items.title: TypeScript upgrade
items.instruction: Upgrade typescript from 5.4 to 5.9 and fix the type errors that appear. Keep runtime behaviour unchanged.
items.rationale: Unknown, cascading errors; one worker iterates on the type checker.

items.title: Three storage adapters plus independent review
items.instruction: Implement three independent storage adapters in src/adapters/s3/, src/adapters/gcs/ and src/adapters/azure/, each implementing the StorageAdapter interface in src/adapters/types.ts (which must not change) with retries, exponential backoff, multipart upload and tests. The user: "When all three are done, have an independent reviewer check them against docs/storage-spec.md before you report."
items.rationale: Three disjoint substantial adapters behind a fixed interface, plus an explicit request for independent review.

items.title: Banker's rounding with an independent check
items.instruction: Change invoice rounding from half-up to banker's rounding (half-even) in src/billing/round.ts and update the tests. The user: "This affects real invoices. I want a second, independent check that totals in fixtures/invoices-10k.json change only where they should."
items.rationale: Explicit request for independent verification of a money change.

items.title: Benchmark three validators
items.instruction: Evaluate three JSON schema validators (ajv, zod, valibot) for our API layer. For each, create bench/<library>/ with its own package.json and a benchmark that validates every payload in fixtures/payloads/ (2,000 files) against schemas/api.json, run it, and write a recommendation with the numbers to docs/validator-choice.md.
items.rationale: Three independent benchmark setups and runs; the recommendation is written after. Separate package environments could also be read as isolation.

items.title: Rate limiting with a fresh reviewer
items.instruction: Implement the rate limiting middleware in src/middleware/rate-limit.ts as specified in docs/rate-limit.md (sliding window per API key, Redis store, 429 with Retry-After) and add tests. After you finish, the user wants a fresh reviewer who has not seen your work to check it against the spec.
items.rationale: Explicit request for an independent reviewer.

items.title: Cache module then three endpoints
items.instruction: Add response caching to the three slowest endpoints (GET /reports, GET /stats, GET /search). There is no cache yet: create src/cache/ with TTL and invalidation hooks first, then use it in the three handlers (about 10 lines each) and add tests.
items.rationale: Trap: the three endpoint changes are small and all depend on the cache module built first.

items.title: Four config flags
items.instruction: Complete four tickets: add the config options maxRetries, timeoutMs, logLevel and region. Each needs validation in src/config/schema.ts, a default in src/config/defaults.ts, an entry in docs/config.md and a test in test/config.test.ts.
items.rationale: Trap: four 'tickets', but every one edits the same four files.

items.title: Plugin registry, plugin and command
items.instruction: Implement (1) a plugin registry in src/plugins/registry.ts, (2) a markdown plugin in src/plugins/markdown.ts that registers through the registry, and (3) a CLI command `plugins list` in src/commands/plugins.ts that prints the registered plugins. Add tests for each.
items.rationale: Trap: three files, but (2) and (3) depend on the registry API created in (1).

items.title: README typo
items.instruction: Fix the typo "recieve" in README.md (two occurrences).
items.rationale: Trivial.
